name: Golimumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection once monthly; IV infusion every 8 weeks (Simponi Aria)
owner: Johnson & Johnson (US and some markets); Merck & Co. (MSD) in Europe

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1κ antibody against TNF-α generated in transgenic mice (Medarex technology).

tagline: Once-monthly human anti-TNF antibody for arthritis and ulcerative colitis
summary: Golimumab is a fully human anti-TNF-α monoclonal antibody given subcutaneously once a month or intravenously every eight weeks. It is used in rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis and ulcerative colitis.
mechanism: Golimumab binds soluble and transmembrane forms of TNF-α with high affinity, preventing receptor binding and reducing markers of inflammation such as CRP, IL-6 and adhesion molecules.
Its long half-life allows monthly subcutaneous dosing.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in April as Simponi for RA, PsA and AS — the first once-monthly TNF inhibitor.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU in October, marketed by Merck/MSD in Europe.

history.title: Ulcerative colitis and IV form
history.detail: Approved for UC; Simponi Aria IV infusion approved for RA.

history.title: IV in PsA and AS
history.detail: Simponi Aria approved for psoriatic arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

history.title: Paediatric arthritis
history.detail: Simponi Aria approved for polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Serious infections (including tuberculosis, invasive fungal and opportunistic infections) and malignancy, including lymphoma.

facts: Commercial rights are split geographically between Johnson & Johnson and MSD.
It was the first TNF inhibitor approved for once-monthly subcutaneous dosing.
